newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat bid limit up, corn and soybeans higher.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat bid limit up, corn and soybeans higher.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures opened up the 20-cent per bushel limit on Monday on reports sub-freezing weekend temperatures in key hard red winter wheat growing regions caused significant crop damage, traders said.
Corn and soybeans also opened higher in fast dealings on spillover strength from wheat.

Record cold in Kansas over the weekend may have caused serious damage to the wheat crop in the southern two-thirds of the state, an agronomist said. Kansas was the largest hard red winter wheat producing state last year.
Bitter cold weather reached as far south as Texas over the weekend, putting crops in Oklahoma and Texas in danger, traders said.

At 0936 CDT, wheat was up 20 to 15 cents per bushel with July bid up the 20-cent limit at $4.28-1/4 a bushel. Corn was 1-3/4 to four cents per bushel higher with May up three at $3.02-1/2. Soybeans were 1-1/2 to seven cents higher with May up 3-1/2 at $8.34.
